courseTitle: World War II & The Home Front (1933–1945)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: WWII & The Home Front
root.gloss: How World War II transformed children’s and families’ lives across Britain and Europe — from evacuation, Kindertransport, and the Blitz to rationing, Bletchley Park, VE Day, and Windermere.

children.label: 1. Outbreak & Child Rescues
children.gloss: From Nazi anti-Jewish laws, Kindertransport suitcases, and Nicholas Winton’s 669 Prague children to Britain’s September 1939 radio outbreak, Blackout, and Operation Pied Piper.

children.label: 1. Outbreak 1939 & Blackout
children.q2Chain: Chamberlain’s 3 Sept 1939 radio broadcast & 38m gas masks → Pitch-dark Blackout curtains & 1.4m ARP wardens
children.gloss: Chamberlain’s 3 Sept 1939 radio broadcast & 38m gas masks → Pitch-dark Blackout curtains & 1.4m ARP wardens

children.label: 3 Sept Broadcast & Gas Masks
children.gloss: After Hitler invaded Poland, Neville Chamberlain announced war on 3 September 1939 and families carried 38 million free gas masks.

children.label: Hitler Invaded Poland 1 Sept 1939
children.gloss: Chamberlain spoke 11:15am by wireless; First London siren sounded minutes.

children.label: 38 Million Free Gas Mask Boxes
children.gloss: Red-and-blue Mickey Mouse toddler masks; Carried cardboard boxes on strings.

children.label: → Switched Off Lights in Blackout
children.gloss: Feared poison gas on towns; War reached ordinary family streets.

children.label: Blackout & 1.4m ARP Wardens
children.gloss: Thick black curtains hid towns from German night bombers while white kerb stripes and 1.4 million ARP wardens guarded dark streets.

children.label: Hide Cities From Night Bombers
children.gloss: Thick black curtains covered windows; Slotted hoods dimmed car headlamps.

children.label: White Kerbs & “Put Light Out!”
children.gloss: 1.4m ARP wardens wore W-helmets; Painted white stripes on kerbs.

children.label: → Triggered Pied Piper Evacuation
children.gloss: Guarded dark streets every night; City children boarded country trains.

children.label: 2. Operation Pied Piper
children.q2Chain: 1.5 million evacuees board trains with luggage labels (1 Sept 1939) → Village hall billeting & mixed country farm lives
children.gloss: 1.5 million evacuees board trains with luggage labels (1 Sept 1939) → Village hall billeting & mixed country farm lives

children.label: 1.5m Evacuees & Coat Labels
children.gloss: Starting on 1 September 1939, Operation Pied Piper sent 1.5 million city children and mothers with pinned luggage labels onto country trains.

children.label: Protect Children From City Bombs
children.gloss: Biggest movement in British history; Walked in school station lines.

children.label: Luggage Labels & Barrier Goodbyes
children.gloss: Carried gas mask and sandwiches; Parents kissed outside station barriers.

children.label: → Lined Up in Village Halls
children.gloss: Rode steam trains to Devon; Met local Billeting Officers next.

children.label: Billeting & Country Farm Life
children.gloss: Volunteer Billeting Officers matched nervous evacuees to rural host families, bringing farm surprises and very mixed experiences.

children.label: Billeting Choice in Village Halls
children.gloss: Spare bedrooms required by law; Siblings hoped not to split.

children.label: Live Cows, Apples & Mixed Homes
children.gloss: First sight of cows, pigs; Warm friendships vs lonely homes.

children.label: Saved Lives When 1940 Blitz Hit
children.gloss: Some returned in Phoney War; Evacuated again during 1940 raids.

children.label: 3. Pre-War Jewish Life & Laws
children.q2Chain: 9m European Jews & ordinary Schultüte childhoods → 400+ Nazi laws & November 1938 Pogrom ban Jewish schoolchildren
children.gloss: 9m European Jews & ordinary Schultüte childhoods → 400+ Nazi laws & November 1938 Pogrom ban Jewish schoolchildren

children.label: Childhoods & Anti-Jewish Laws
children.gloss: Jewish children once carried sweet-filled Schultüte cones to school, until Hitler’s 1933 Nazi Party passed over 400 unfair laws.

children.label: 9m Citizens & Schultüte Cones
children.gloss: Doctors, shops, football, scout groups; Children carried sweet Schultüte cones.

children.label: 400+ Laws & 1935 Nuremberg Laws
children.gloss: Stripped German Jews’ citizenship rights; Banned parks, pools, bicycles, pets.

children.label: → Escalated to November 1938 Pogrom
children.gloss: Boycotted Jewish shops April 1933; Cut families off from neighbours.

children.label: Kristallnacht & School Expulsion
children.gloss: During the violent November 1938 Pogrom (Kristallnacht), gangs burned synagogues and banned all Jewish children from German state schools.

children.label: Synagogues Burned & 30,000 Arrested
children.gloss: Smashed thousands of shop windows; Arrested 30,000 Jewish men.

children.label: 15 Nov: Banned From State Schools
children.gloss: Jewish teachers sacked from classrooms; Forced pupils onto separate benches.

children.label: → Sparked 1938 Kindertransport Rescue
children.gloss: Terrified parents sought foreign safety; Shocked British newspapers and MPs.

children.label: 4. The Kindertransport Rescue
children.q2Chain: Parliament admits 10,000 unaccompanied children → Nine-year-old Vera’s one small suitcase to Liverpool Street Station
children.gloss: Parliament admits 10,000 unaccompanied children → Nine-year-old Vera’s one small suitcase to Liverpool Street Station

children.label: 10,000 Children & £50 Sponsors
children.gloss: After Kristallnacht, Parliament sped up permits for nearly 10,000 unaccompanied child refugees backed by £50 British sponsors.

children.label: Charities Begged MPs After Pogrom
children.gloss: Jewish and Quaker charities begged MPs; Sped permits for under-seventeens.

children.label: Jewish and Quaker charities begged MPs
children.gloss: Jewish and Quaker charities begged MPs

children.label: 10,000 Rescued Without Parents
children.gloss: Parents forbidden to travel alongside; Needed £50 British care sponsor.

children.label: → Families Packed One Small Suitcase
children.gloss: Left Germany, Austria, Prague, Poland; Raced before September 1939 war.

children.label: Vera’s Suitcase to Liverpool St
children.gloss: Nine-year-old Vera Löwyová packed her diary and porcelain doll in Prague, sailing from the Hook of Holland to London foster care.

children.label: Vera’s Diary & Porcelain Doll
children.gloss: Nine-year-old waved at Prague station; One small suitcase, ten Reichsmarks.

children.label: Dutch Hot Chocolate to Harwich
children.gloss: Kind women served hot chocolate; Ferry to Harwich, London fosterers.

children.label: Saved 10,000 Young Lives
children.gloss: Borders slammed shut September 1939; Vera never saw parents again.

children.label: 5. Winton & 669 From Prague
children.q2Chain: Winton cancels skiing trip & works with Warriner & Chadwick → Eight Prague trains save 669 children & 1988 scrapbook reunion
children.gloss: Winton cancels skiing trip & works with Warriner & Chadwick → Eight Prague trains save 669 children & 1988 scrapbook reunion

children.label: Prague Upstanders & Rescue Team
children.gloss: Cancelling his Swiss ski trip, Nicholas Winton teamed up with Doreen Warriner, Trevor Chadwick, and mother Babi to rescue Prague children.

children.label: Martin Blake’s Urgent Prague Call
children.gloss: Cancelled Switzerland skiing holiday; Chose upstander over quiet bystander.

children.label: Warriner, Chadwick & Mother Babi
children.gloss: Chadwick led children past guards; Babi pressed Home Office visas.

children.label: → Organised Eight Prague Trains
children.gloss: Printed children’s photos in papers; Found £50 sponsors and homes.

children.label: 669 Saved & 1988 Attic Scrapbook
children.gloss: Eight trains brought 669 children safely to London before war stopped the ninth train; fifty years later, Winton’s attic scrapbook reunited them.

children.label: Eight Trains Saved 669 Children
children.gloss: Included Vera’s May 1939 train; 1 Sept war stopped ninth.

children.label: Grete Found 1939 Attic Scrapbook
children.gloss: Kept secret nearly fifty years; Saved adults stood on BBC.

children.label: Proved One Team’s Moral Courage
children.gloss: Listed all 669 rescued names; Inspired classrooms around the world.

children.label: 2. Blitz, Rations & War Work
children.gloss: Through 57 straight nights of the Blitz and U-boat blockades, British families sheltered underground, grew Dig for Victory veg, worked in factories, and cracked Enigma.

children.label: 6. The Blitz & Raid Shelters
children.q2Chain: Black Saturday starts 57 nights of bombing & Anderson/Morrison shelters → 150,000 on Tube platforms & volunteer firewatchers
children.gloss: Black Saturday starts 57 nights of bombing & Anderson/Morrison shelters → 150,000 on Tube platforms & volunteer firewatchers

children.label: 57 Blitz Nights & Home Shelters
children.gloss: From Black Saturday (7 Sept 1940), bombers hit London for 57 nights plus UK cities while families used Anderson and Morrison shelters.

children.label: Black Saturday & Industrial Cities
children.gloss: Bombed London 57 straight nights; Hit Coventry, Liverpool, Hull, Belfast.

children.label: Garden Anderson & Table Morrison
children.gloss: 2m steel Andersons under soil; Indoor steel-mesh Morrison table cages.

children.label: → 150,000 Slept Deep in Tube
children.gloss: Firewatchers saved St Paul’s dome; Shielded families from bomb blasts.

children.label: Tube Platforms & Fire Volunteers
children.gloss: Over 150,000 Londoners slept on bunk-fitted Tube platforms while AFS firefighters, rooftop firewatchers, and WVS canteens worked overhead.

children.label: 150,000 on Bunk-Bed Tube Platforms
children.gloss: Queued with blankets, tea flasks; Triple bunks and lending libraries.

children.label: AFS, Stirrup Pumps & WVS Tea
children.gloss: Sandbags doused rooftop incendiary bombs; WVS mobile canteens rehoused families.

children.label: Civilian Teamwork Refused Surrender
children.gloss: Kept ports and factories running; Meanwhile U-boats threatened food ships.

children.label: 7. Rationing & Dig for Victory
children.q2Chain: Atlantic U-boats sink food ships & Jan 1940 ration books → 1.4m Dig for Victory allotments & healthier British children
children.gloss: Atlantic U-boats sink food ships & Jan 1940 ration books → 1.4m Dig for Victory allotments & healthier British children

children.label: U-Boats & Fair-Shares Coupons
children.gloss: Because German U-boats sank Atlantic food ships, the Ministry of Food launched coupon ration books in January 1940 for fair shares.

children.label: U-Boats Sank 70% Imported Food
children.gloss: Hunted merchant convoys in Atlantic; Stopped rich hoarding scarce food.

children.label: One Egg, 50g Butter & Coupons
children.gloss: Two bacon rashers, tinned Spam; Green books gave cod-liver oil.

children.label: → Families Planted Every Spare Lawn
children.gloss: Home-grown veg stayed unrationed; Launched nationwide Dig for Victory.

children.label: 1.4m Allotments & Potato Pete
children.gloss: Families dug 1.4 million allotments — even in the Tower of London moat — and ate Woolton Pie, helping children grow taller and healthier.

children.label: Tower Moat & 1.4m Allotments
children.gloss: Dug parks, greens, school fields; Planted Tower of London moat.

children.label: Doctor Carrot & Woolton Pie
children.gloss: Carrot fudge replaced rationed sweets; Oatmeal root-veg Lord Woolton Pie.

children.label: Children Grew Taller & Healthier
children.gloss: Less sugar, more fresh veg; Women Land Girls harvested farms.

children.label: 8. Women at War (1941–1945)
children.q2Chain: Dec 1941 National Service Act & 80,000 Land Girls / Lumberjills → Munitions Canary Girls & 168 ATA Spitfire ferry pilots
children.gloss: Dec 1941 National Service Act & 80,000 Land Girls / Lumberjills → Munitions Canary Girls & 168 ATA Spitfire ferry pilots

children.label: 1941 Call-Up & 80,000 Land Girls
children.gloss: Parliament’s December 1941 National Service Act called up unmarried women aged 20–30 as 80,000 Land Girls and Lumberjills supplied Britain.

children.label: Dec 1941 Conscription Aged 20–30
children.gloss: Millions of men fought overseas; Princess Elizabeth trained in ATS.

children.label: 80,000 Land Girls & Lumberjills
children.gloss: Ploughed wheat, milked cows, rats; Felled pines for mine props.

children.label: → Kept Food & Factories Running
children.gloss: Beat Atlantic U-boat blockade shortages; Nearly 1m entered shell factories.

children.label: Canary Girls & Spitfire Pilots
children.gloss: Munitions workers risked yellow-staining TNT blasts while 168 female ATA pilots like Maureen Dunlop ferried Spitfires and Lancasters.

children.label: Yellow TNT Skin & Wooden Shoes
children.gloss: Packed explosive TNT and cordite; Wore wooden soles, zero hairpins.

children.label: 168 ATA Pilots & Equal Pay
children.gloss: Flew Spitfires using paper maps; Won equal ATA pay 1943.

children.label: Transformed Views of Women’s Work
children.gloss: Mastered heavy engineering and flight; 7,500 women also ran Bletchley.

children.label: 9. Codebreakers at Bletchley
children.q2Chain: 158m-million-million Enigma settings vs Turing’s Bombe at Station X → 7,500 secret women & Ultra shorten war by two years
children.gloss: 158m-million-million Enigma settings vs Turing’s Bombe at Station X → 7,500 secret women & Ultra shorten war by two years

children.label: Enigma vs Alan Turing’s Bombe
children.gloss: German Enigma rotors reset every midnight; building on Polish breakthroughs, Alan Turing and Gordon Welchman built the Bombe at Station X.

children.label: Enigma Reset Every Midnight
children.gloss: Spinning rotors and front plugboard; 158 million million million settings.

children.label: Turing’s Bombe & Flowers’s Colossus
children.gloss: Polish clues helped Station X; Tommy Flowers built computer Colossus.

children.label: → Steered Convoys Past U-Boats
children.gloss: Used daily German weather clues; Needed 10,000 round-the-clock staff.

children.label: 7,500 Women & 30-Year Secret
children.gloss: Three-quarters of Bletchley’s 10,000 staff were women who kept Ultra secret until the 1970s and shortened WWII by at least two years.

children.label: 75% Women Wired Bombe Drums
children.gloss: Naval Wrens worked eight-hour shifts; Logged signals, translated German codes.

children.label: Official Secrets Kept Until 1970s
children.gloss: Never even told their parents; Ultra intelligence guided D-Day plans.

children.label: Shortened War by Two+ Years
children.gloss: Saved millions of wartime lives; Helped bring May 1945 victory.

children.label: 3. VE Day, Healing & Memory
children.gloss: Victory in Europe on 8 May 1945 brought joyful street parties, the 1948 NHS, autumn poppy remembrance, and gentle Lake District healing for 300 orphaned Windermere Children.

children.label: 10. VE Day, NHS & Remembrance
children.q2Chain: VE Day street parties (8 May 1945) & 1948 NHS rebuilding → Whitehall Cenotaph, two-minute silence & red poppies today
children.gloss: VE Day street parties (8 May 1945) & 1948 NHS rebuilding → Whitehall Cenotaph, two-minute silence & red poppies today

children.label: 8 May 1945 VE Day & NHS
children.gloss: Churchill’s 8 May 1945 radio broadcast sparked street parties, followed by rebuilding 2 million bombed homes and founding the 1948 NHS.

children.label: 8 May Bunting & Street Parties
children.gloss: Churchill waved near Trafalgar Square; Fought on until August VJ.

children.label: Commonwealth Losses & 1948 NHS
children.gloss: 2m homes bombed; rationing 1954; Built prefabs, free 1948 NHS.

children.label: → Pledged Lasting November Memory
children.gloss: Mourned 447,000 UK dead, Commonwealth; Honoured sacrifices each autumn.

children.label: The Cenotaph & Red Poppies
children.gloss: Each 11 November and Remembrance Sunday, crowds keep a two-minute silence at the Whitehall Cenotaph wearing red poppies.

children.label: Whitehall Cenotaph (“Empty Tomb”)
children.gloss: Gathers on 11 November, Sunday; Honours everyone across UK memorials.

children.label: 11am Silence & Red Poppies
children.gloss: Kept quiet two-minute 11am silence; Bloomed on muddy WWI battlefields.

children.label: Passes Peace Duty to Youth
children.gloss: Remembers ordinary wartime courage; Links to survivor voices next.

children.label: 11. The Windermere Children
children.q2Chain: Ten RAF Stirling bombers fly 300 orphaned survivors from Prague (Aug 1945) → Calgarth red bicycles & The ’45 Aid Society
children.gloss: Ten RAF Stirling bombers fly 300 orphaned survivors from Prague (Aug 1945) → Calgarth red bicycles & The ’45 Aid Society

children.label: RAF Airlift & Calgarth Healing
children.gloss: On 14 August 1945, ten RAF bombers flew 300 orphaned Holocaust child survivors from Prague to heal beside Lake Windermere.

children.label: 10 RAF Bombers Carried 300 Youth
children.gloss: Funded by Central British Fund; Flew Prague to Cumbria Windermere.

children.label: Bread Under Pillows & Red Bikes
children.gloss: Dr Friedman, Marie Paneth listened; Swam lake; rode red bicycles.

children.label: → Rebuilt Trust & Lifelong Family
children.gloss: Starved children hid bread slices; English lessons and art healed.

children.label: ’45 Aid Society & Living Voices
children.gloss: Calling themselves “The Boys”, survivors like Sir Ben Helfgott and Arek Hersh founded The ’45 Aid Society and shared memories in schools.

children.label: “The Boys” & Sir Ben Helfgott
children.gloss: Became doctors, teachers, Olympic lifter; Stayed lifelong friends together.

children.label: 1963 Charity & School Talks
children.gloss: Started ’45 Aid Society charity; Helped Tom Palmer’s book.

children.label: Kept Real Eyewitness Voices Alive
children.gloss: Arek Hersh, Sam Laskier spoke; Thanked Britain through kindness.
